crossRefs.note: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father; but a foolish son brings grief to his mother.
A wise son listens to his father’s instruction, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
Poverty and shame come to him who refuses discipline, but he who heeds correction shall be honored.
He said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.
After this, Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.
Now, my son, may Yahweh be with you and prosper you, and build the house of Yahweh your God, as he has spoken…
You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for…
David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed; for Yahweh God…
The ear that listens to reproof lives, and will be at home among the wise.
He who refuses correction despises his own soul, but he who listens to reproof gets understanding.
Turn at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my spirit on you. I will make known my words to you.
For the commandment is a lamp, and the law is light. Reproofs of instruction are the way of life,
Listen to counsel and receive instruction, that you may be wise in your latter end.
As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
Let the righteous strike me, it is kindness; let him reprove me, it is like oil on the head; don’t let my head refuse…
This testimony is true. For this cause, reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
Say these things and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.

translations.web: A fool despises his father’s correction, but he who heeds reproof shows prudence.
translations.bsb: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
translations.kjv: A fool despiseth his father's instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent.
translations.asv: A fool despiseth his father's correction; But he that regardeth reproof getteth prudence.
